metadata.title: ChronoScope: Time-Series Diagnostics and Forecast Evaluation
metadata.description:
ChronoScope connects time-series diagnostics, numerical implementations and finite forecast comparisons to their source observations and information cutoffs. This technical report derives the forecasting and diagnostic methods, specifies the artifact contracts, and distinguishes retained experiments from current numerical execution. It documents the published ForecastScope provider, prefix-only normalization, constant-input policies and eighteen bilingual lessons with actual model references and browser training.

The external combination experiment finds lower mean MASE for temporally validated mixtures than for a recency-only control on eligible M4 Weekly and M3 Monthly series. AutoTheta retains lower monthly point error and lower interval score on both collections. On fifteen selected blocks, the planned Timestral-209M minus AutoTheta mean MASE difference is -0.44740, with a descriptive case-reweighting interval from -0.79356 to -0.15991. A separate synthetic confirmation preserves the browser point map and reduces mean normalized interval score from 4.749003 to 2.393376 on 800 fresh series; marginal coverage is 82.73 percent at the nominal 80 percent level. Unfavorable fixed-context, selector and ridge results remain reported.

Complete forecasts, source and checkpoint identities, generated tables and independent scoring make the comparisons inspectable. The results concern their admitted cases, protocols and sampling units. They establish neither general forecasting superiority, authentic-data calibration nor an accepted operational policy. Source code and computational records accompany the report.

metadata.version_notes: Documents published numerical-provider separation, observable-unit and exact-constant policies, full-precision transport, eighteen executable lessons and actual seven-model references. Reconciles current method equations with retained historical implementations; preserves all historical results and their source identities. Titles and conclusions remain bounded to diagnostics and finite forecast evaluation.
